title: Fitness/outdoor training
description: You will need your own mat for your training. If you want, you can also bring a drinking bottle with you - we hope you have a lot of fun during your training.

title: Wednesday meeting
description: Friends from Ruggell – Wuarscht n'Brot from Ruggell provide the best entertainment with their music and charm. A cozy and sociable program with friends from the neighboring community.

title: Exchange on the sofa
description:
We would like to stay in conversation with you. With our new format “Exchange on the Sofa” we are creating an additional offer for open encounters in a cozy atmosphere.
Here you can raise your concerns early, address your own topics or simply listen. Without a program, without registration – just come along and talk to community leader Johannes Hasler on the “sofa in the Grossabünt”. The Grossabünt offers the perfect environment for this – before the respective Wednesday meetings.

title: Summer party for those staying at home
Stefan Kainbacher. Trialogue: Holobiont Habitat – Chapter 1. Decode
location:
Kunstraum Engländerbau (Lageplan)
Städtle 37
9490 Vaduz
Fürstentum Liechtenstein, Vaduz
description:
An expansive audiovisual installation about the possibilities and limits of communication between biological and technical actors.

Trialogue: Holobiont Habitat – Chapter 1: Decode is an expansive audiovisual installation about the possibilities and limits of communication between biological and technical actors.

At the center of the art space are eight black 19-inch server racks, arranged in a circle like a technological Stonehenge. The racks form the habitat of a hybrid organism in which plants, sensors, computers, artificial intelligence and audiovisual systems are connected.

Each rack houses live plants, full-spectrum grow lights, speakers, and various technical components. Network cables, power lines and hoses of an automated irrigation system connect the individual units into a common circuit. The technical infrastructure intentionally remains visible and becomes part of the spatial composition.

The plants are continuously recorded using various sensors. The focus is on measuring bioelectrical signals using Plant SpikerBox systems, supplemented by environmental and climate data. Four of the experimental stations also have camera systems with which the plants can be visually observed.

The collected data is processed by a locally operated multi-agent system. The AI ​​agents analyze electrical activity patterns, image data and environmental parameters and try to recognize connections, states and recurring patterns in the behavior of the plants. The installation stages this process not as a solved problem, but as an ongoing attempt at a machine approach to a non-human form of communication.

The work is seen as an artistic research setting: The AI ​​does not try to control plants, but rather to understand them. The actual topic of the work is less the plant itself and more the question of how technical systems create meaning and what limits exist.

Trialogue: Holobiont Habitat – Chapter 1: Decode marks the first part of an ongoing series of works. While this chapter addresses the question of decoding biological signals, future chapters will examine additional forms of interaction, translation, and coexistence between human and non-human actors.
